Public safety power shutoffs (PSPS) events: research motivation

Research motivation:

  • Wildfires have been increasing in frequency and intensity
  • Wildfire smoke is associated with adverse health outcomes
  • One cause of wildfires are power lines
  • Power outages are associated with adverse health outcomes

An important mitigation strategy for higher wildfire risk rolled out in California and increasingly adopted in other states is public safety power shutoffs (PSPS), which are planned power outages to prevent power lines from causing fires.

However, PSPS events are implemented during times of high wildfire risk, and are thus likely to co-occur with the very thing they are trying to prevent: wildfire smoke.

Public safety power shutoffs (PSPS) events: research questions

  • What are the effects of PSPS events on adverse health outcomes?
  • What is the extent of dual wildfire smoke-PSPS exposure?
  • What is the association between this dual exposure and adverse health outcomes?

Type Data Coverage Years
Exposure Public safety power shutoff (PSPS) data, PSE Event, circuit-level data from the three major utility providers in CA (PGE, SDG&E, SCE) 2013-2022

Outcome Hospital and emergency department data, California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) Daily, zip-code level visits 2013-2019


  • Study population: Adults (18+) in California
  • Study period: 2013-2019
  • Study design: Time-stratified case-crossover design
  • Statistical analysis: Conditional logistic regression
